note: Only what an organisation publishes itself. Amounts only as published; null means not published.

items.name: Austrian Film Institute (Österreichisches Filminstitut, ÖFI)
items.summary: Austria's national funding body for cinema films, in Vienna. It funds script and project development, production, distribution and festival participation of fiction, documentary and animated films, including Austrian shares of co-productions.
items.eligibility: Production companies with a current filmography. First-time producers get dedicated support. Co-productions qualify for the Austrian share.
items.how_to_apply: Online application by the published submission dates, with a production-ready script, budget and financing plan. Projects are decided in the following session.
items.budget_note: Federal contribution of EUR 36.5 million to ÖFI plus EUR 2.5 million to ÖFI+ in 2026 (published)

items.name: Austrian Television Fund (Fernsehfonds Austria)
items.summary: Fund at the Austrian media regulator RTR in Vienna that gives grants for the production and exploitation of TV films, documentaries and series by independent Austrian producers.
items.eligibility: Independent Austrian film producers, with TV broadcasters taking part in the financing.
items.how_to_apply: Application to RTR under the published guidelines, decided by RTR's managing director after consulting a review board.
items.budget_note: Annual budget of EUR 13.5 million (published)

items.name: Cine Tirol Production Incentive
items.summary: Film commission and fund of Tyrol in Innsbruck. For selected cinema, TV and streaming projects shot in Tyrol it gives non-repayable production grants, within the available budget.
items.how_to_apply: Mandatory information call, then application via the Cine Tirol submission tool before shooting starts.

items.name: Cinestyria Film Commission and Fund
items.summary: Film commission and fund of Styria in Graz. It gives non-repayable production grants for film and TV projects that spend money in Styria, plus support for regional festivals.
items.eligibility: Qualified and experienced film producers, with a regional spend of at least 150% of the grant.
items.how_to_apply: Written application to Cinestyria with script or treatment, budget showing the Styrian spend and other funding, by the published deadlines.
items.budget_note: Grants up to 20% of total project costs (published)

items.name: City of Vienna Cultural Department film funding (MA 7)
items.summary: Film funding of the City of Vienna's cultural department (MA 7), alongside the Vienna Film Fund. It supports experimental films, documentaries, shorts and feature films shot mainly in Vienna.
items.eligibility: Adults with main residence in Vienna, or sole traders, companies and partnerships based in Vienna.
items.how_to_apply: Online application form (with or without ID Austria), with fixed annual windows for production funding.

items.name: Land Salzburg commercial film funding
items.summary: Economic film funding of the state of Salzburg for cinema and TV films, series, animation, virtual production and streaming formats that shoot in Salzburg and spend money with the local film industry.
items.eligibility: Film producers and screenwriters (people, companies and partnerships) running a production in Salzburg with shooting days and local spend.
items.how_to_apply: Application by the published submission dates (10 September and 27 October 2026).
items.budget_note: Direct grant up to 10% of total net production costs, capped at 100% of the Salzburg film industry spend and 65% of the Salzburg spend (published)

items.name: Lower Austria film funding (Land Niederösterreich)
items.summary: Film funding of the state of Lower Austria for productions with a link to the state or shot there, covering cinema fiction and documentaries, TV productions, shorts and art films.
items.eligibility: Film productions with a content or personal link to Lower Austria, or made there. A regional spend of 100% (documentary) or at least 150% (fiction and TV series) of the award applies.
items.how_to_apply: PDF form or online application. Shorts and art films any time, feature-length and TV projects by the expert panel's published deadlines.

items.name: Upper Austria cultural film funding (Land Oberösterreich)
items.summary: Cultural film funding of the state of Upper Austria in Linz for artistic fiction, documentary, short, experimental and animated films and series, from project development through production to release and festivals.
items.eligibility: Mainly filmmakers from Upper Austria, or projects dealing with Upper Austria in at least half of their running time.
items.how_to_apply: Online form. Requests up to EUR 15,000 go to the culture department, larger ones to the Upper Austrian film commission by its published dates.

items.name: Vienna Film Fund (Filmfonds Wien)
items.summary: Vienna's film fund. It funds project development, production of cinema films, children's and documentary films, TV films and fiction series, plus cinema releases and festival participation, with a link to the Vienna film industry.
items.how_to_apply: Application by the published submission dates under the fund's guidelines.
items.budget_note: Production funding up to EUR 700,000 per cinema film, development up to EUR 50,000 (films) or EUR 75,000 (series), fiction series up to EUR 330,000 per season. City funding of EUR 12.5 million in 2026 (published)

items.name: Beside Productions (Beside Tax Shelter)
items.summary: Belgian coproducer near Brussels with an in-house Tax Shelter fund that collects money from Belgian companies and invests it in European films and series that spend part of their budget in Belgium.
items.eligibility: European works under the AVMS Directive with planned Belgian spend.
items.how_to_apply: Schedule a call, Beside checks eligibility, estimates Belgian spend and commits Tax Shelter financing.
items.budget_note: Around EUR 30 million of Tax Shelter funds a year (published)

items.name: Centre du Cinéma et de l'Audiovisuel (Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles)
items.summary: Film body of the French-speaking community of Belgium in Brussels. Its film commission supports writing, development and production of fiction and animation features and shorts and documentaries, a separate commission funds TV series, and it also supports promotion and distribution.
items.eligibility: Production companies and other audiovisual operators of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, see the general provisions.
items.how_to_apply: Dossier through the Subside platform, the film commission meets three times a year (February, May and October).

items.name: Creative Europe MEDIA
items.summary: The European Union's programme for the audiovisual sector. Gives grants for the development of European films, TV series, documentaries and video games, for cross-border co-development and for the promotion and distribution of European works.
items.eligibility: Organisations from countries taking part in Creative Europe, as set out in each call for proposals.
items.how_to_apply: Competitive calls for proposals on the European Commission's Funding and Tenders portal, with fixed submission windows (annual or twice a year).
items.budget_note: Creative Europe programme 2021 to 2027 budget €2.44 billion, all strands together (published)

items.name: Flanders Audiovisual Fund (Vlaams Audiovisueel Fonds, VAF)
items.summary: Film body of the Flemish Community in Brussels. Its film fund supports fiction, animation, documentary and experimental films of all lengths, its media fund supports TV series made with Flemish broadcasters, and its game fund supports video games, from scriptwriting and development to production.
items.eligibility: Applicants based in Flanders or Brussels, foreign coproductions need at least 50 percent of financing in place.
items.how_to_apply: Applications by published deadlines, examined by reading committees and ratified by the board.

items.name: SCOPE Invest
items.summary: Brussels tax shelter intermediary that has published an FSMA-approved prospectus since 2007. It raises Belgian Tax Shelter money from companies for audiovisual and stage works and says it has helped finance more than 250 feature films.
items.eligibility: Works eligible under the Belgian Tax Shelter, produced or coproduced through a Belgian production company.
items.how_to_apply: Contact SCOPE Invest directly.

items.name: Screen Flanders
items.summary: Economic support measure of the Flanders government, run by the VAF, for fiction, animation and documentary features and series that spend part of their budget in the Flanders Region, aimed largely at international coproductions.
items.eligibility: Belgian producers, foreign producers via a coproduction with a Belgian producer who meets the criteria. Assessment is selective and mainly on economic criteria.
items.how_to_apply: Two calls a year (2026 deadlines: 6 March and 4 September), online application.
items.budget_note: Annual budget EUR 3.5 million, maximum EUR 400,000 per project as refundable advances on net receipts (published)

items.name: screen.brussels fund
items.summary: Economic fund of the Brussels-Capital Region that since 2016 invests in films, animation, documentaries, series and web series, VR, games and audio formats that spend part of their budget in Brussels.
items.eligibility: Commercial production companies established in Belgium, with minimum eligible spend in the Brussels-Capital Region and a share of financing secured.
items.how_to_apply: Meet the team, register in the professionals database, then apply online for one of three sessions a year (January, May, September).

items.name: Taxshelter.be (Shelter Prod)
items.summary: Brussels tax shelter intermediary that raises investment from Belgian companies for films, series, performing arts and games under the Belgian Tax Shelter, under an FSMA prospectus. Producers can register on the site.
items.eligibility: Productions eligible for the Belgian Tax Shelter.
items.how_to_apply: Producers register through the producer form on the site.

items.name: Umedia (uFund)
items.summary: Brussels coproduction company that raises Belgian Tax Shelter money through its uFund offer and uses it to finance and co-produce around 50 European feature films, animation projects and series a year, also offering physical production services.
items.eligibility: European producers who coproduce with Umedia in Belgium.
items.how_to_apply: Contact Umedia directly.
items.budget_note: EUR 35 million of Tax Shelter funds, around 50 projects a year (published)

items.name: Wallimage
items.summary: Economic audiovisual and games fund of Wallonia, based in Mons with an office in Liège. Wallimage Coproductions co-finances around fifty films, series and other formats a year, Belgian or international with a Belgian coproducer, that spend in Wallonia.
items.eligibility: Independent Belgian production companies active for at least one year, Walloon spending above EUR 300,000 (EUR 75,000 for a documentary) and over 30 percent of financing secured.
items.how_to_apply: Four competitive sessions a year (usually January, March, June and September) via the online application, prior contact advised.
items.budget_note: EUR 5.5 million a year for coproductions (published)

items.name: Bulgarian National Film Center (Национален филмов център, NFC)
items.summary: Bulgaria's national film agency in Sofia. Expert commissions select projects for state support for development and production of features, short fiction, documentaries, animation and series, minority co-productions, local distribution and promotion.
items.eligibility: Companies registered under Bulgarian law and registered as producers, distributors or exhibitors with the NFC.
items.how_to_apply: Competitive sessions, two deadlines a year for features, documentaries and animation and four for minority co-productions.

items.name: City of Zagreb, audiovisual (film) programme
items.summary: The City of Zagreb's yearly call for public needs in culture includes support for film production: short fiction, animated and experimental films and documentaries.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly public call for programmes of public needs in culture of the City of Zagreb.
items.budget_note: About EUR 200,000 for 24 film projects in 2026 (published)

items.name: Croatian Audiovisual Centre (Hrvatski audiovizualni centar, HAVC)
items.summary: Croatia's national agency for the audiovisual sector in Zagreb, funded by the state and by broadcasters and operators. It funds development and production of Croatian features, first features, documentaries, animation, shorts and experimental films, and minority co-productions.
items.eligibility: Croatian producers, and foreign films with a Croatian minority co-producer under a bilateral treaty or the European Convention.
items.how_to_apply: Calls open through the year for most schemes, minority co-production with yearly submission deadlines.

items.name: Istria County film co-financing (Istarska županija, Regione Istriana)
items.summary: Yearly public call of Istria County, run with the Croatian Audiovisual Centre, that co-finances short fiction, documentary, experimental and animated films by Istrian authors or inspired by Istria and shot at Istrian locations.
items.eligibility: Producers registered in Croatia or in the HAVC producer register, independent artists, and producers applying with a director. Funding for one film per applicant, finished by 15 December.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly public call with an application form on the county website (the 2026 call was published on 28 January 2026).
items.budget_note: EUR 57,300 from Istria County plus EUR 40,000 from HAVC for 2026 (published)

items.name: Czech Audiovisual Fund (Státní fond audiovize, SFA)
items.summary: Czechia's national fund in Prague, created in 2025 from the State Cinematography Fund. Four councils award selective support to Czech audiovisual works from first script draft through production to distribution, covering cinema, TV works, animation and video games.
items.eligibility: Czech and foreign applicants under the terms of each call, mostly for Czech audiovisual works and minority co-productions.
items.how_to_apply: Calls with fixed submission windows set in the yearly short-term concept, forms downloaded from the Výzvy section.
items.budget_note: Total allocation of calls for 2027 CZK 787,500,000 (published)

items.name: Olomouc Region cinema support (Podpora kinematografie, Olomoucký kraj)
items.summary: Grant title of the Olomouc Region that encourages filmmakers to shoot in the Jeseníky and Central Moravia tourist areas and to use local services.
items.eligibility: Productions shooting in the Jeseníky and Central Moravia areas, eligible applicants as listed in the rules.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly grant call, 2026 applications from 12 to 26 January via the region's RAP system.

items.name: Plzeň Region audiovisual programme (Podpora tvorby audiovizuálních děl v Plzeňském kraji)
items.summary: Plzeň Region grant programme for the production and preparation of features, shorts, documentaries, series and student films shot at least partly in the region or about people linked to it.
items.eligibility: Projects made at least partly in the Plzeň Region or about people connected to it. Up to three applications per applicant.
items.how_to_apply: Through the eDotace application, 2026 window 16 January to 30 April.
items.budget_note: CZK 50,000 to 2,000,000 per project, at most 10% of total costs (student films CZK 20,000 to 50,000) (published)

items.name: South Bohemian Region audiovisual grants (Jižní Čechy Film Office)
items.summary: Individual grants from the South Bohemian Region for fiction films, series, animation and documentaries shot in the region, run with the South Bohemia Film Office. Paid after the costs are incurred.
items.eligibility: Companies or individuals based in Czechia with a project that includes shooting in South Bohemia and has confirmed distribution.
items.how_to_apply: Register the project (1 March to 31 May 2026), then apply (1 June to 31 October 2026).
items.budget_note: CZK 300,000 to 1,200,000 per project, at most 30% of eligible costs (published)

items.name: South Moravian Region audiovisual programme (Jihomoravský filmový nadační fond)
items.summary: Support for audiovisual work made in Brno and the South Moravian Region. The film foundation set up by Brno and the region has been replaced in 2026 by a regional grant programme for fiction, documentary and animated works.
items.eligibility: Natural or legal persons as defined in the programme, with a link to Brno and South Moravia and at least 10% own contribution.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly grant programme of the South Moravian Region, 2026 applications from 4 to 29 May via the region's data box.
items.budget_note: CZK 19,000,000 for the 2026 programme, maximum CZK 5,000,000 per project (published)

items.name: Ústí Region film vouchers (Filmové vouchery, Ústecký kraj)
items.summary: EU Just Transition funded vouchers from the Ústí Region for feature films and documentaries for cinema and for TV or online fiction and documentary series, covering part of the costs spent in the region.
items.eligibility: Small and medium-sized companies with a Czech producer involved and eligible costs in the Ústí Region.
items.how_to_apply: Rolling applications to the Ústí Region until the project ends (31 December 2027).
items.budget_note: CZK 50,000,000 in total, vouchers of CZK 500,000 to 2 million (features), 250,000 to 1 million (documentaries) and 1 to 3.5 million (TV and online) (published)

items.name: Vysočina Film Office (Vysočina Tourism)
items.summary: Film office of the Vysočina Region. Instead of a cash grant it signs cooperation agreements and pays for services during the shoot in Vysočina, such as locations and accommodation, for features, documentaries, series, shorts and student films.
items.eligibility: Projects shooting in the Vysočina Region, with minimum shooting days or lengths per format.
items.how_to_apply: Request for cooperation with a project presentation, 2026 deadline 2 March, decisions by 31 March.
items.budget_note: CZK 2,500,000 for 2026 (published)

items.name: Zlín Region audiovisual programme (Program na podporu audiovizuální tvorby ve Zlínském kraji)
items.summary: Grant programme of the Zlín Region for audiovisual production in the region, opened every two years. Recent awards went to fiction features, animation and documentaries.
items.how_to_apply: Online application during the programme window (19 January to 20 March 2026 for KUL04-26).
items.budget_note: Allocation CZK 12 million for KUL04-26 (published)

items.name: Danish Film Institute (Det Danske Filminstitut)
items.summary: The state film body of Denmark, in Copenhagen. Through several schemes it funds the development and production of Danish features, documentaries, shorts and TV drama, and supports a few minority co-productions each year.
items.eligibility: Danish film professionals and production companies. Minority co-productions apply through a Danish co-producer.
items.how_to_apply: Through the DFI support portal (Støtteportalen), with terms and deadlines per scheme.

items.name: Den Vestdanske Filmpulje (West Danish Film Fund)
items.summary: Regional film fund of a group of West Danish municipalities, with its office in Filmby Aarhus. It supports the development and production of films, series and documentaries made in its area, and animated and live action shorts through calls.
items.eligibility: Professional film and TV productions in the member municipalities of the fund.
items.how_to_apply: In application periods through the application portal. Live action shorts only through one or two calls a year.

items.name: FilmFyn
items.summary: Regional film fund for Funen (Fyn), based in Faaborg. It invests in the development and production of Danish features, animation, documentaries and TV series with a Funen link, and in minority co-productions with foreign lead producers.
items.eligibility: Projects with creative or production roots on Funen. Minority projects apply through the Danish co-producer. No support for shorts or TV programmes at present.
items.how_to_apply: No fixed deadlines, start with an initial contact through the application portal, about six weeks to a final decision.

items.name: Cultural Endowment of Estonia, Audiovisual Arts Endowment (Eesti Kultuurkapital)
items.summary: Public endowment in Tallinn whose audiovisual arts branch funds the scripts, development and production of Estonian features, documentaries, short films and animation, and minority co-productions at half the usual maximum.
items.eligibility: Legal persons whose main activity is film production, with at least 10% cost-sharing or co-financing.
items.how_to_apply: Four deadlines a year (20 February, 20 May, 20 August, 20 November).
items.budget_note: Feature production up to EUR 200,000, feature documentary up to EUR 50,000, short fiction up to EUR 40,000, animation up to EUR 4,000 per minute and EUR 150,000 in total (published)

items.name: Estonian Film Institute (Eesti Filmi Instituut)
items.summary: National foundation in Tallinn funded by the Ministry of Culture. It supports Estonian feature, documentary and animated films from script to release, TV documentary series in post-production, cinema distribution, and minority co-productions with a foreign lead producer.
items.eligibility: Estonian film producers. Minority co-production support needs a foreign lead producer and an Estonian release within a year of the premiere.
items.how_to_apply: In application rounds with published deadlines.

items.name: AVEK (Promotion Centre for Audiovisual Culture)
items.summary: Part of the Finnish copyright organisation Kopiosto, funded mainly from private copying compensation in the state budget. It supports new Finnish documentaries, animation, short films and media art, with script grants for individuals and production support for companies.
items.eligibility: Script and project grants for individuals and working groups, support for audiovisual works for production companies.
items.how_to_apply: Online application. Applications for audiovisual works are closed from 1 November 2026 to 13 January 2027.

items.name: Finnish Film Foundation (Suomen elokuvasäätiö)
items.summary: The state-funded film foundation of Finland, in Helsinki. It gives script grants, development, slate and production support for fiction films, series and documentaries, production support for international co-productions, and marketing and distribution support.
items.eligibility: Film professionals and companies registered in Finland. Scriptwriting grants go to professional writers with a Finnish bank account.
items.how_to_apply: Through the online application system, after registering (can take up to a week), in rounds set out in each grant announcement.

items.name: IPR.VC
items.summary: Alternative investment fund manager in Helsinki and London that invests money from institutional investors in film and TV. It works through long-term alliances with established studios and producers rather than single-project financing.
items.eligibility: Established companies with an international footprint, a verifiable commercial track record and experienced management. No one-off single-project financing.
items.how_to_apply: By contact with the company.

items.name: Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes Cinéma
items.summary: Coproduction fund of the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region (Lyon). It co-produces feature films and TV series, one-offs and animation specials with a strong link to the region, and supports writing and development.
items.eligibility: Producers of projects with a significant link to the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region (article 2.1 of its rules).
items.how_to_apply: Application to an expert committee that meets two to three times a year, see the committee calendar.
items.budget_note: Coproduction investment averages EUR 220,000 per film, development support capped at EUR 20,000 per project, around EUR 3 million a year for cinema and EUR 2 million for TV (published)

items.name: Bourgogne-Franche-Comté Region film and audiovisual creation and production fund
items.summary: Regional fund of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté for writing, development and production of long fiction, documentaries and short films, aimed at creation in the region and at bringing shoots to it. Production associations can get support for shorts.
items.eligibility: Authors writing projects linked to the region, and production companies (or production associations for shorts) developing or shooting in Bourgogne-Franche-Comté.
items.how_to_apply: Fixed submission windows, for long fiction 1 to 31 March and 1 to 30 November each year, followed by a reading committee.

items.name: Ciclic Centre-Val de Loire
items.summary: Regional agency of Centre-Val de Loire for books, film and image. It gives grants for writing, development and production of documentaries, fiction features, animation features and series, short films and TV fiction, plus international co-development.
items.eligibility: Production companies and authors, several schemes require a company based in Centre-Val de Loire or a link with the region.
items.how_to_apply: Per scheme in the Ciclic aid catalogue, with set committee dates.

items.name: City of Paris short film support fund (Mission Cinéma)
items.summary: Fund of the City of Paris film office, created in 2006, for the production of short films by French production companies.
items.eligibility: Film or audiovisual production companies established in France acting as producer or majority coproducer.
items.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply through the City of Paris online service for short films.

items.name: CNC (Centre national du cinéma et de l'image animée)
items.summary: The French state body for film and moving image. It supports writing, development, production, distribution and export of feature films, documentaries, animation and series, through automatic support and selective schemes such as the avance sur recettes.
items.eligibility: Producers, directors and authors, depending on the scheme. Many schemes require a French production company.
items.how_to_apply: Per scheme on cnc.fr, selective aid is decided by the CNC president after advice from expert commissions.

items.name: Cofiloisirs
items.summary: Paris finance house, backed by BNP Paribas, that lends to film and TV producers, distributors and cinemas. It structures credit for development, preparation and production, including long-running animation series and international coproductions.
items.eligibility: Producers, distributors and cinema operators in France and abroad.
items.how_to_apply: Contact the team directly, a credit committee meets weekly.

items.name: Collectivité de Corse film and audiovisual aid fund
items.summary: Selective fund of the Corsican regional authority (Ajaccio) for writing, development and production of feature films, TV films and series, documentaries, short films, animation and new-media works.
items.eligibility: Authors, directors and production companies as set out in the culture aid rules, with a link to Corsica.
items.how_to_apply: Complete dossier by fixed deadlines, three technical committees a year (2026 deadlines: 2 January, 30 April, 31 July).

items.name: Eurimages (Council of Europe)
items.summary: The Council of Europe's cinema fund in Strasbourg, with 39 member states plus Canada. Supports the co-production of fiction, animation and documentary features of at least 70 minutes between producers from member states, plus distribution and exhibition.
items.eligibility: At least two co-producers from different member states of the Fund, within set minimum and maximum shares of the co-production budget.
items.how_to_apply: Online application in one of three calls per year, see the published deadlines. Projects are assessed by co-production working groups of external experts.

items.name: Grand Est Region film, audiovisual and animation fund
items.summary: Fund of the Grand Est region (Strasbourg) with the CNC for writing, development and production of feature films, shorts, animation, genre films and TV and new-media documentary and fiction shot in the region.
items.eligibility: Production companies committing regional spending of at least 160 percent of the regional aid, shooting or editing must not have started when applying.
items.how_to_apply: Calls for projects twice a year (15 November and 30 April for features), reviewed by a consultative committee of professionals.
items.budget_note: Up to EUR 300,000 for a live-action fiction feature and EUR 100,000 for a feature documentary (published)

items.name: IFCIC (Institut pour le financement du cinéma et des industries culturelles)
items.summary: Paris credit institution set up by the French state and banks that guarantees bank loans and lends directly to cultural companies, including film and TV producers, distributors and exporters, mostly with public money.
items.eligibility: Cultural and creative companies within the scope of the French Ministry of Culture, in France and Europe.
items.how_to_apply: Directly with IFCIC or through the company's bank for a guarantee.

items.name: Île-de-France Region film and audiovisual support fund (Fonds de soutien cinéma et audiovisuel)
items.summary: Fund of the Île-de-France region (Paris area) for feature films, international coproductions and TV and web works in fiction, animation and documentary, plus screenwriting aid and post-completion aid for films.
items.eligibility: Production companies, with separate strands for French-majority films and minority international coproductions.
items.how_to_apply: Selective, applications in sessions on a published calendar, live-action films must register before the first day of shooting.

items.name: Logical Content Ventures
items.summary: Paris investment fund, launched in 2021, through which private and institutional investors finance a diversified catalogue of French and international films and series.

items.name: Lucy Finance (SOFICA manager)
items.summary: Paris film finance adviser that manages SOFICAs, which invest tax-advantaged private savings in French film and audiovisual production and recoup from the works' revenues. It also offers script assessment and outsourced finance services to producers.
items.eligibility: Mainly French independent production, as required for SOFICA investment.
items.how_to_apply: Contact Lucy Finance through its website.
items.budget_note: More than EUR 120 million invested through its SOFICAs (published)

items.name: Natixis Coficiné
items.summary: Specialist credit institution in Paris, part of Natixis (Groupe BPCE), that lends to film and TV producers, distributors and cinemas, and since 2018 to games companies. It works across Europe and in several countries outside it.
items.eligibility: Producers, distributors, cinema operators and technical industries, in France and internationally.
items.how_to_apply: Contact the Coficiné team directly.

items.name: Normandie Images
items.summary: Film agency of the Normandy region in Rouen. It supports writing, development and production of feature films, shorts, TV fiction, documentary and animation, with production aid tied to spending in Normandy.
items.eligibility: Production companies, feature films must be eligible for CNC approval and show planned spending in Normandy of at least 100 to 160 percent of the aid.
items.how_to_apply: Applications per session, decisions voted by the Normandy Region permanent commission and published per session.
items.budget_note: EUR 100,000 to 200,000 for a fiction or animation feature, EUR 50,000 to 100,000 for a feature documentary (published)

items.name: Nouvelle-Aquitaine film and audiovisual fund (Région Nouvelle-Aquitaine with ALCA)
items.summary: Support fund of the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region, run with the regional agency ALCA in Bordeaux. It funds writing, development, production and international coproduction of feature films, shorts, documentaries, animation and TV works made in the region.
items.eligibility: Production companies, production aid requires regional spending of at least 100 to 160 percent of the aid depending on the format.
items.how_to_apply: Online application in fixed deposit sessions, the next session opens 11 January 2027.

items.name: Occitanie Region audiovisual creation aid (Aide à la création audiovisuelle)
items.summary: Support of the Occitanie region (Toulouse and Montpellier) for fiction, documentary, animation and XR projects, from rewriting and development through pilots to production, for shorts, features and TV works.
items.eligibility: Projects that meet the eligibility guide of the scheme, assessed by separate fiction, animation and documentary committees.
items.how_to_apply: Dossier per genre with fixed deadlines several times a year (for example 1 December 2026 for documentary and fiction features).

items.name: Pays de la Loire Region film, audiovisual and digital creation fund
items.summary: Fund of the Pays de la Loire region (Nantes), run with the CNC. It supports production of feature films, TV fiction, documentaries, short films and digital works, and development such as pilots, script rewrites and project development.
items.eligibility: Companies and associations, projects are judged by technical committees against regional priorities.
items.how_to_apply: Online application with three deadlines a year (in 2026: 9 February, 26 May and 5 October).

items.name: Pictanovo (Hauts-de-France)
items.summary: Film and audiovisual agency of the Hauts-de-France region, based in Tourcoing. It runs funds for feature films and TV fiction, animation, documentary, short films, web works, immersive projects and games, plus an economic fund for productions with high regional spending.
items.eligibility: Producers and authors with projects linked to the Hauts-de-France region, conditions differ per fund.
items.how_to_apply: Each project starts with a meeting with the fund manager, then goes to an independent reading committee.
items.budget_note: EUR 8.6 million invested each year (published)

items.name: PROCIREP (Société des producteurs de cinéma et de télévision)
items.summary: French producers' collecting society that funds creation from private copy levies. Its cinema commission supports writing and development of features and production of shorts, its television commission supports documentary, fiction, animation and live performance programmes.
items.eligibility: French production companies, TV aid needs a French broadcaster commitment and financing in place as set out per scheme.
items.how_to_apply: Applications to the cinema or television commission by published deadlines, twice a year for cinema.
items.budget_note: Feature writing aid EUR 12,000 to 63,000 per company (50 percent repayable), average TV aid EUR 6,500 per 52 minutes (published)

items.name: Région Sud Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur film and audiovisual support fund
items.summary: Fund of the Région Sud (Marseille) with the CNC for writing, development and production of TV fiction, documentaries, animation, short films and immersive works, with extra support for international coproduction projects in development.
items.eligibility: Mainly production companies, the delegated producer must hold most of the rights for development aid.
items.how_to_apply: Online application on the region's aid portal, in calls with set deadlines.
items.budget_note: Up to EUR 100,000 for a TV single drama and EUR 150,000 for a TV series, development aid up to EUR 15,000 to 20,000 (published)

items.name: SOFICA Cineaxe
items.summary: SOFICA that invests private savings, which carry a 48 percent income tax reduction, in French and European film and audiovisual production and development, chosen by an investment committee of industry experts.
items.how_to_apply: Download and send the production or development application file from the producers page.

items.name: SOFICA Cinécap
items.summary: SOFICA co-founded by BNP Paribas and Cinécapital that invests tax-advantaged private savings in French feature films and audiovisual works with partner production companies.

items.name: SOFICA Cinémage
items.summary: SOFICA that raises money from private investors with a French income tax reduction and invests it in French-language films, TV documentaries, animation and development companies, with a focus on first and second films and independent producers.
items.eligibility: Works of original French expression, or another language if the majority coproducer comes from a country with a coproduction treaty with France.
items.how_to_apply: Submit a project for the next investment committee by its deadline, TV documentaries are reviewed on a rolling basis.
items.budget_note: Cinémage 21 raised EUR 12.45 million in 2025 (published)

items.name: SOFICA Cineventure
items.summary: Paris SOFICA set up by Apple Juice that invests money from private shareholders, who receive a tax reduction, in film and TV series production and in development with producers.
items.how_to_apply: Send the project form and listed documents to the Cineventure team.
items.budget_note: EUR 35.2 million raised since creation (published)

items.name: SOFICA Cofinova
items.summary: SOFICA that collects private savings with a French tax reduction and invests in cinema films, TV fiction, animated series and TV documentaries, and finances development of projects, in return for rights to revenues.
items.eligibility: Projects submitted by producers, assessed on artistic quality and commercial potential.
items.how_to_apply: Projects go to Cofinova investment committees of industry professionals.

items.name: SOFICA Indéfilms
items.summary: SOFICAs raised by public offering whose sole purpose is financing French and European films and audiovisual works, with a stated focus on independent cinema.
items.eligibility: French and European film and audiovisual works.
items.how_to_apply: Application file for the committee calendar published in the producers section.

items.name: SOFICA Palatine Etoile (Cine Nomine)
items.summary: SOFICAs founded in 2003 by the producers of Cine Nomine with Banque Palatine (BPCE group) to invest tax-advantaged private savings in French and European cinema.

items.name: SOFICA Sofitvciné
items.summary: SOFICAs whose sole purpose is financing French and European cinema and TV works. Through production subsidiaries they also fund development (rights, writing, casting), recouped with a premium when the work goes into production.
items.eligibility: Works of original French expression for cinema or TV, or in the language of a majority coproducer from the European Community.
items.how_to_apply: Email producer and project details to receive the application file and committee calendar.
items.budget_note: Sofitvciné 14 has share capital of EUR 11 million (published)

items.name: Strasbourg Eurométropole film and audiovisual production fund
items.summary: Production fund of the Strasbourg Eurométropole for fiction, animation and documentary works for cinema, TV, web and transmedia that make a significant part of the work in the Strasbourg area. In 2024 it backed documentaries, TV series, animation, shorts and features.
items.eligibility: The delegated production company, for TV projects the producer with a French broadcaster commitment or applying for CNC support.
items.how_to_apply: Three deposit dates a year (15 November, 15 March and 15 June).

items.name: Bayerischer BankenFonds (BBF, LfA Förderbank Bayern)
items.summary: Bank fund in Munich, run through the LfA Förderbank Bayern, that co-finances cinema films and distribution projects already recommended for funding by FFF Bayern, with conditionally repayable loans at market interest and a share in revenues.
items.eligibility: Cinema productions and distribution projects with a funding recommendation from FFF Bayern and expected commercial success.
items.how_to_apply: Through FFF Bayern, after its funding recommendation.
items.budget_note: Up to 100% of the recommended FFF award, at most EUR 1 million for production or EUR 200,000 for distribution (published)

items.name: FFF Bayern (FilmFernsehFonds Bayern)
items.summary: Bavaria's film and media fund in Munich. It funds treatments, scripts, project development, cinema and TV films, series, web series, XR and distribution, mostly as conditionally repayable loans with a spend requirement in Bavaria.
items.eligibility: Producers with a registered office, branch or permanent establishment in Germany. International co-productions need a German producer, and at least 150% of the award should be spent in Bavaria.
items.how_to_apply: Online application portal for the four award sessions a year, after contacting the responsible funding officer. Cinema films need a German distribution deal, TV projects a broadcaster deal.
items.budget_note: Cinema film production up to 30% of eligible costs with a maximum of EUR 3 million, TV series up to EUR 1 million. Total funding volume over EUR 40 million (published)

items.name: Film- und Medienstiftung NRW
items.summary: North Rhine-Westphalia's film and media fund in Düsseldorf. It funds feature films, documentaries, series, games and audio from treatment and script through pre-production, production and post-production to distribution and world sales.
items.eligibility: German producers, with a German co-producer for international projects. Low-budget grants (total costs up to EUR 1.5 million) are for producers and directors based in NRW.
items.how_to_apply: Online application portal by the published deadlines, after a mandatory advice meeting at least one week before the deadline.
items.budget_note: Cinema production funding up to 50% of costs as an interest-free conditionally repayable loan, low-budget grants up to 80% of costs (published)

items.name: German Federal Film Board (FFA Filmförderungsanstalt)
items.summary: Germany's federal film body in Berlin. Since 2025 it also runs the jury-based federal cultural film funding, with grants for scripts, project development, production of features, documentaries and shorts, distribution and co-productions.
items.eligibility: Producers with residence or registered office in Germany, or a German branch for companies based elsewhere in the EU or EEA. Talent films (first and second features) go to the Kuratorium junger deutscher Film.
items.how_to_apply: Online via the FFA service portal by the published submission dates for each jury session, with webinars and individual advice up to two weeks before the deadline.
items.budget_note: Jury-based production funding up to EUR 1 million per feature film and up to EUR 500,000 per feature documentary (published)

items.name: HessenFilm und Medien
items.summary: Hesse's film fund in Frankfurt, owned by the state and Hessischer Rundfunk. It funds film and series from treatment through production and post-production to distribution, with a focus on talent and documentaries.
items.eligibility: Producers from Germany, including German co-producers of international co-productions.
items.how_to_apply: Online funding application by the published submission dates, decided by juries.
items.budget_note: Up to EUR 1 million per project, with a regional spend of 100% to 125% of the award (published)

items.name: ILB and IBB interim financing of film productions
items.summary: Joint programme of the state development banks of Brandenburg (ILB, lead) and Berlin (IBB): loans and guarantees to cash-flow film and TV productions against broadcaster commissions, co-productions and distribution or sales guarantees.
items.eligibility: Production companies based in Berlin or Brandenburg, or German producers with a project in the region, including start-ups with enough production experience.
items.how_to_apply: Informal application to ILB or IBB, or via Medienboard Berlin-Brandenburg, with the documents on the bank's checklist.
items.budget_note: Loans and guarantees up to EUR 3.75 million, usually at least EUR 100,000 (published)

items.name: Investitionsbank Sachsen-Anhalt (IB ProMi)
items.summary: State development bank of Saxony-Anhalt in Magdeburg. Its IB ProMi programme lends to experienced production companies to close financing gaps on cinema films and high-end TV productions, usually together with a commercial bank.
items.eligibility: Film production companies with at least two commercially successful feature films and a measurable economic effect in Saxony-Anhalt. Foreign companies need a branch in Germany.
items.how_to_apply: Application to the Investitionsbank, with credit and project risk assessment and application fees as published.
items.budget_note: Loans up to 30% of total project costs, minimum EUR 250,000 and maximum EUR 3 million (published)

items.name: Kuratorium junger deutscher Film
items.summary: Foundation in Wiesbaden, financed by all German states, that has run the national talent film funding since 2026: script and project development and production of first and second feature films, documentaries and shorts, including children's films.
items.eligibility: Talent film projects, meaning fiction or documentary films up to the director's second feature-length film.
items.how_to_apply: Application with the forms and guidelines on the website, by the published submission deadline for each funding line.
items.budget_note: Up to EUR 25,000 for script development, EUR 50,000 for project development, EUR 500,000 for a feature film and EUR 40,000 for a short film. Annual budget over EUR 9 million (published)

items.name: Medienboard Berlin-Brandenburg
items.summary: Joint film fund of Berlin and Brandenburg, based in Potsdam-Babelsberg. It funds project and script development, cinema and TV films, high-end series, experimental and talent films, digital production and distribution, mainly as success-dependent loans.
items.how_to_apply: Application forms on the website, submitted by the published submission and decision dates.

items.name: Medienförderung RLP
items.summary: Media fund of Rhineland-Palatinate in Mainz, a subsidiary of the state media authority, backed by the state, SWR and ZDF. It gives grants for films, series, videos, audio and games, from concept and script to production and release.
items.eligibility: Authors, developers, producers, distributors and publishers with a cultural link to Rhineland-Palatinate (seat or branch there, or content tied to the state), with 120% of the grant spent in the state.
items.how_to_apply: Mandatory first advice call, then online registration and application with a short pitch video, by the published deadline of each funding round.

items.name: MFG Baden-Württemberg Filmförderung
items.summary: Film funding arm of the Baden-Württemberg media company in Stuttgart. It funds scripts, pre-production, production of cinema and TV films and series, and distribution, with a focus on animation, VFX and young documentary makers.
items.eligibility: Producers can apply for production funding.
items.how_to_apply: Online via the MFG database by the end of the published submission period, plus a signed paper form within five working days.
items.budget_note: Annual film funding budget of about EUR 15 million (published)

items.name: Mitteldeutsche Medienförderung (MDM)
items.summary: Joint film and media fund of Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia, based in Leipzig. It funds development, production and distribution of feature films, documentaries, animation, children's films, TV events and series, shorts, games and XR.
items.eligibility: Production companies. Feature films need a German producer and proven German distribution, and funds should mostly be spent in the region.
items.how_to_apply: Advice meeting at least 14 days before the submission date, then online application via the Mitteldeutsches Antragsportal (MAP).
items.budget_note: Shareholder funding of EUR 19.31 million in total (2025) (published)

items.name: MOIN Filmförderung Hamburg Schleswig-Holstein
items.summary: Film fund of Hamburg and Schleswig-Holstein, with offices in Hamburg and Kiel. It supports feature films, documentaries, animation, high-end series, shorts and XR from first treatment through production to release and festivals.
items.eligibility: Producers can apply for production funding. Projects should use Hamburg or Schleswig-Holstein as locations and local crews and facilities.
items.how_to_apply: Online only, after an advice meeting at least 14 days before the deadline. Separate committees and dates for higher-budget projects, lower-budget projects, shorts and innovative formats. Development goes through the NEST portal.
items.budget_note: Funded by Hamburg (EUR 14.6 million), Schleswig-Holstein (EUR 1.2 million), NDR, ZDF and other sources (published)

items.name: MV Filmförderung
items.summary: Film fund of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania in Schwerin. It funds script and project development, production, distribution and presentation of cinema and TV films, series and other audiovisual works.
items.how_to_apply: Applications at three fixed submission dates a year, decided by a committee. Small requests up to EUR 5,000 have extra dates.
items.budget_note: Production funding up to 50% of eligible costs, at most EUR 250,000 per project, as a conditionally repayable loan, or as a grant for low-budget documentaries and features (published)

items.name: nordmedia (Film- und Mediengesellschaft Niedersachsen/Bremen)
items.summary: Film and media fund of Lower Saxony and Bremen, based in Hanover. It funds script and project development, production of cinema, TV and streaming fiction and documentaries, games and distribution, mainly as success-dependent repayable loans.
items.how_to_apply: Online advice meeting in the published advice window, where applicants get the code for the digital submission, then submission by the published deadline.
items.budget_note: Production funding up to 50% of total costs, 60% for international co-productions with partners from more than one EU state and up to 80% for difficult works (published)

items.name: Hellenic Film and Audiovisual Center (EKKOMED)
items.summary: Greece's national film body in Athens, which also runs the Greek cash rebate. Its selective schemes fund screenwriting, development and production of features and first films, shorts, micro-budget work, completed films, XR projects and minority co-productions.
items.eligibility: Depends on the scheme. The minority co-production scheme is for foreign film projects with a Greek co-producer.
items.how_to_apply: Through the EKKOMED e-services portal during the published calls, several schemes have more than one call a year.
items.budget_note: Minority co-production, first call of 2026: EUR 620,000 in total, EUR 30,000 to EUR 100,000 per project. Short film, call 2026A: EUR 30,000 to EUR 35,000 per project (published)

items.name: National Film Institute Hungary (Nemzeti Filmintézet, NFI)
items.summary: Hungary's national film body in Budapest. Its selective funding covers script development, pre-production, production and marketing of Hungarian and co-produced films and series for cinema and TV, plus distribution of cinema releases.
items.eligibility: Hungarian or co-production projects for cinema or media services. Since 24 July 2026 the development, pre-production and production calls are withdrawn while interim committees work, distribution and marketing applications are still accepted.
items.how_to_apply: Online through the NFI MOTOR application system, rolling or periodic as set in each call.

items.name: Icelandic Film Centre (Kvikmyndamiðstöð Íslands)
items.summary: Public body in Reykjavík that runs the Icelandic Film Fund. It gives grants for screenwriting, development, production, post-production and promotion of Icelandic features, shorts, documentaries and TV fiction, and supports minority co-productions.
items.eligibility: Only companies registered in Iceland can receive funding. Projects need a connection to Iceland.
items.how_to_apply: Grants can be applied for at any time of the year.

items.name: Arts Council of Ireland (Reel Art)
items.summary: Ireland's public arts funding body in Dublin. Its Reel Art scheme pays for creative and experimental documentaries on artistic subjects, made by individual film artists for cinema exhibition.
items.eligibility: Individual film artists and organisations, as set out in the yearly Reel Art guidelines.
items.how_to_apply: Online application during the yearly call. Guidelines appear about two weeks before the scheme opens.
items.budget_note: Maximum award €120,000 (published)

items.name: Coimisiún na Meán (Sound & Vision Scheme)
items.summary: Ireland's media regulator in Dublin runs the Sound & Vision Scheme, funded by the TV licence fee, which pays for TV, radio and film programmes on Irish culture, history and language that will be broadcast in Ireland.
items.eligibility: Broadcasters and independent producers with programming for national, local or community TV and radio services in Ireland.
items.how_to_apply: Applications in funding rounds, several each year, as announced on the Sound & Vision industry page.

items.name: Screen Ireland (Fís Éireann)
items.summary: Ireland's national screen agency, based in Galway. Funds development, production and distribution of Irish live action and animated features, documentaries, TV drama and animated series, plus creative co-productions with an Irish partner.
items.eligibility: Irish writers, directors and production companies, and Irish producers involved creatively as minority partner in official co-productions.
items.how_to_apply: Online application by the published deadline of each scheme, after reading the development, production and distribution guidelines.
items.budget_note: Development up to €125,000 per project, Irish fiction production up to €1,300,000 per film, creative co-productions normally up to €350,000 (published)

items.name: WRAP Fund (Western Region Audiovisual Producers Fund)
items.summary: Commercial fund for the West of Ireland (Clare, Donegal, Galway, Leitrim, Mayo, Roscommon, Sligo) that invests in film, TV, animation and games productions with significant work in the region, and in regional production companies.
items.eligibility: Producers of film, TV, games or animation with a significant amount of production work in the WRAP region.
items.how_to_apply: Initial enquiry by email to the WRAP Executive, who sends guidelines. Eligible applications are generally accepted on a rolling basis.
items.budget_note: Up to €200,000 per production (published)

items.name: Apulia Film Commission (Apulia Film Fund)
items.summary: Regional foundation in Bari that runs the Apulia Film Fund for features, series, creative documentaries, animation and shorts, plus a separate development fund for projects linked to Apulia.
items.eligibility: Micro, small and medium enterprises whose main activity is film and video production (ATECO 59.11).
items.how_to_apply: Online through the commission's application platform, the 2026 call runs until 2 November 2026.
items.budget_note: Apulia Film Fund 2026: EUR 5 million in total, up to EUR 320,000 for a feature, EUR 450,000 for a series, EUR 500,000 for animation and EUR 120,000 for a documentary (published)

items.name: Banca Etica (Tax Credit Cinema)
items.summary: Cooperative bank in Padua that buys the film tax credits of small independent producers, so they get the cash straight away, and offers credit lines to film and audiovisual companies.
items.eligibility: Small independent film production, executive production and post-production companies whose tax credit has been recognised by the Ministry, with better terms for members of Banca Etica and CNA Cinema e Audiovisivi.

items.name: Directorate-General for Cinema and Audiovisual (DGCA, Ministero della Cultura)
items.summary: The film directorate of the Italian Ministry of Culture in Rome. Besides automatic support and the tax credit, it runs selective grants for writing, development, production and distribution, plus bilateral co-development and co-production funds and a fund for minority co-productions.
items.eligibility: Selective support is awarded per support line (writing, development, production, Italian and international distribution), with separate bilateral funds with France, Tunisia, Portugal and the Baltic states.
items.how_to_apply: Through the calls published per support line on the DGCA website.

items.name: Emilia-Romagna Film Commission (Regional Audiovisual Fund)
items.summary: Audiovisual fund of the Emilia-Romagna region in Bologna, set up under regional law 20/2014, with yearly calls for development, production and promotion.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly public calls for development and production, no call open at the time of checking.

items.name: Film Commission Regione Campania (Piano Cinema Campania)
items.summary: Film commission of the Campania region in Naples. Under regional law 30/2016 it runs the yearly Piano Cinema with grants for producing and promoting film and audiovisual work.
items.how_to_apply: Online through the Piano Cinema platform, the 2026 window ran from 31 August to 30 September 2026.

items.name: Fondazione Sardegna Film Commission
items.summary: Regional foundation in Cagliari that runs grants for large fiction productions, Sardinian themed fiction and documentaries, plus hospitality and city funds for shoots in Sardinia.
items.eligibility: Italian and European production and distribution companies. Cultural associations and freelancers are excluded.
items.how_to_apply: Applications by certified email (PEC) to the published calls, the Fondo Grandi Produzioni 2025 to 2026 closed on 4 March 2026.
items.budget_note: Fondo Grandi Produzioni: up to EUR 500,000 per project, at most 50% of eligible costs (published)

items.name: Fondo per l'Audiovisivo del Friuli Venezia Giulia
items.summary: Regional fund in Friuli Venezia Giulia that supports training, project development and distribution for independent audiovisual companies and professionals from the region.
items.eligibility: Independent production companies and audiovisual professionals.
items.how_to_apply: Three call windows in 2026 (10 March to 1 April, 3 to 30 June, 14 September to 8 October).

items.name: FVG Film Commission (FVG Film Fund)
items.summary: Production fund of Friuli Venezia Giulia, run from Trieste, for fiction, series, documentaries and shorts that shoot in the region. The grant is a share of the money spent in the region.
items.eligibility: Italian, EU and non EU film and video production companies (ATECO 59.11 or 59.12), as producer, co-producer or executive producer, applying before the shoot.
items.how_to_apply: Three deadlines a year (28 February, 30 June, 30 September), decision within 30 days.
items.budget_note: Up to 30% of the spend in the region, with a maximum of EUR 350,000 for fiction and series and EUR 40,000 for documentaries and shorts (published)

items.name: IDM Film Fund South Tyrol (IDM Südtirol)
items.summary: Film fund of the province of South Tyrol, run by IDM in Bolzano. It funds production preparation, production and short films for film and TV projects developed, produced or shot in South Tyrol.
items.eligibility: Film and TV projects developed, produced or shot in South Tyrol that spend the funding locally.
items.how_to_apply: Online application with fixed submission deadlines each year.

items.name: Lombardia per il Cinema (Regione Lombardia and Lombardia Film Commission)
items.summary: Production grants of the Lombardy region for features, animation, series and documentaries shot in Lombardy, plus a development call for writing and pre-production run with Lombardia Film Commission.
items.eligibility: Micro, small and medium film production companies (ATECO 59.11) with at least two years of activity and two filed accounts. The grant covers at most 50% of the production costs in Lombardy.
items.how_to_apply: Online through the Regione Lombardia calls portal. The second production call closed on 22 January 2026, the development call runs from 31 July to 15 October 2026.
items.budget_note: Second production call: EUR 3,000,000 in total, up to EUR 250,000 for a feature and EUR 300,000 for a series (published)

items.name: Piemonte Film TV Fund (Regione Piemonte and Film Commission Torino Piemonte)
items.summary: Non repayable grants from the Piedmont region, presented by Film Commission Torino Piemonte in Turin, for film, TV and animation productions, with separate development, documentary and short film funds.
items.eligibility: Companies working in audiovisual, film and television production.
items.how_to_apply: Calls, rules and deadlines are published on the Regione Piemonte website.
items.budget_note: EUR 7 million a year under the 2021 to 2027 programme (published)

items.name: Regione Lazio Cinema and Audiovisual Fund (Lazio Cinema International)
items.summary: Film funds of the Lazio region around Rome: Lazio Cinema International for international co-productions, Lazio Cinema Futuro for independent local producers, plus screenwriting and short film calls.
items.eligibility: Lazio Cinema International is for international co-productions of features, TV works and series, Lazio Cinema Futuro for independent producers from the region.
items.how_to_apply: Several application windows a year, the first 2026 window of Lazio Cinema International opened on 12 March 2026.
items.budget_note: Lazio Cinema International: EUR 5 million per window (published)

items.name: Regione Toscana production fund (Toscana Film Commission and Sviluppo Toscana)
items.summary: Calls of the Tuscany region, managed by Sviluppo Toscana and promoted by Toscana Film Commission in Florence, with grants for shorts, documentaries, features and series made in Tuscany.
items.eligibility: Micro, small and medium film and audiovisual production companies from Italy, Europe or outside Europe.
items.how_to_apply: Online through the Sviluppo Toscana system during the call, the 2024 call closed on 5 February 2025.
items.budget_note: 2024 call: EUR 4,000,000 in total (published)

items.name: Sicilia Film Commission
items.summary: Film office of the Sicilian region in Palermo. It runs a public call with grants for film and audiovisual productions in Sicily for 2025 to 2027, including documentaries and TV series.
items.how_to_apply: Through the public call (Avviso Pubblico) for 2025 to 2027 published on the commission's website.

items.name: Trentino Film Commission (Trentino Film Fund)
items.summary: Film fund of the province of Trento for features, TV fiction and documentaries shot in Trentino, from development to distribution, with extra points for green productions.
items.eligibility: Italian, EU and non EU production companies, plus local professionals and broadcasters. Spend in Trentino must be at least 150% of the grant for films and 120% for documentaries, and the grant is at most 50% of the budget.
items.how_to_apply: Through the Agora platform or certified email, with deadlines on 3 March, 9 June and 22 September 2026.
items.budget_note: Up to EUR 400,000 for features and TV productions, up to EUR 40,000 for documentaries (published)

items.name: Umbria Film Commission (Umbria Film Fund)
items.summary: Regional fund in Umbria for films, TV series, documentaries and shorts, open to national and international productions and to Umbrian companies, financed by the regional EU development programme.
items.eligibility: National and international productions and Umbrian film and audiovisual companies.
items.budget_note: EUR 4,000,000 for 2026 and 2027, up to EUR 250,000 for a feature and EUR 350,000 for a series set entirely in Umbria (published)

items.name: Veneto Film Commission (Regione Veneto production and development funds)
items.summary: Production and development funds of the Veneto region for features, series, animation, documentaries, shorts and XR works with a minimum spend in Veneto.
items.eligibility: Film production SMEs (ATECO 59.11) based in the EU, as sole producer, co-producer or executive producer. Minimum spend in Veneto of EUR 150,000 (features, series, animation) or EUR 20,000 (documentaries, shorts, XR).
items.how_to_apply: Through the Regione Veneto online portal in two windows (12 May to 30 June 2026 and 1 December 2026 to 2 February 2027).
items.budget_note: Production fund 2026: EUR 3.68 million, up to EUR 250,000 for a feature and EUR 350,000 for a series. Development fund 2026: EUR 100,000 (published)

items.name: National Film Centre of Latvia (Nacionālais kino centrs)
items.summary: State body in Riga that administers the state budget for film. It runs production competitions for Latvian feature, documentary and animated films (including animated series) and a support competition for minority co-productions.
items.eligibility: Registered Latvian film producers.
items.how_to_apply: Annual production competitions with public project presentations and expert commissions.
items.budget_note: EUR 1,257,775 for new film production in the 2026 competition (published)

items.name: State Culture Capital Foundation (Valsts kultūrkapitāla fonds)
items.summary: Latvian public culture fund with a film arts section. It funds scriptwriting and development of feature, documentary and animated films, and production of short fiction, short animation and documentaries that have no production support from the National Film Centre.
items.eligibility: No production funding for feature-length fiction or animation, or for projects with National Film Centre production support.
items.how_to_apply: Regular project competitions on a published schedule.

items.name: Lithuanian Film Centre (Lietuvos kino centras)
items.summary: State institution in Vilnius under the Ministry of Culture. It funds scripts, development and production of Lithuanian feature, documentary, animated and interactive films, short films and series, minority co-productions, and the distribution of Lithuanian films.
items.eligibility: Legal persons whose main activity is film production, registered in the EU or EEA, with a Lithuanian entity or branch at payment. Broadcasters cannot apply.
items.how_to_apply: In calls listed in the general funding calendar.

items.name: Film Fund Luxembourg (Fonds national de soutien à la production audiovisuelle)
items.summary: Public body of Luxembourg that funds film, TV and platform projects through its Selective Financial Aid (AFS) for writing, development, production and majority or minority coproduction, plus author grants, promotion and distribution aid, and game preproduction calls.
items.eligibility: Luxembourg production companies, 50 percent of financing confirmed at submission and the full aid spent in Luxembourg.
items.how_to_apply: Application per scheme, decisions by a five-member selection committee.
items.budget_note: AFS production aid up to EUR 1,500,000 per project, international coproduction of a documentary up to EUR 290,000, as advances on receipts (published)

items.name: Frysk Filmfûns (Frisian Film Fund)
items.summary: Film fund of the province of Friesland (Leeuwarden) for short films, development of series, features, documentaries and animation with Frisian roots, and a production incentive for film and TV shoots in Friesland.
items.eligibility: Projects rooted in Friesland in language, landscape or culture, the production incentive is open to regional, national and international productions shooting in Friesland.
items.how_to_apply: Application form in rounds, the next deadline is 1 October 2026, then 1 April 2027.
items.budget_note: Maximum EUR 30,000 for shorts, EUR 25,000 for development and EUR 40,000 for the production incentive (published)

items.name: Hubert Bals Fund (IFFR)
items.summary: Fund of International Film Festival Rotterdam that supports feature film projects by filmmakers from countries where local funding is lacking, from script development to post-production, plus schemes for European minority coproducers and Dutch producers.
items.eligibility: Filmmakers from countries on the HBF eligible list, European minority producers for HBF+Europe, Dutch producers for the NFF+HBF scheme.
items.how_to_apply: Per scheme by published deadlines, see the practical info and deadlines page.

items.name: IDFA Bertha Fund
items.summary: Fund of the IDFA documentary festival in Amsterdam for documentary projects from Africa, Asia, Eastern Europe, Latin America, the Caribbean and Oceania, with a European minority coproduction scheme for European producers.
items.eligibility: Directors from listed countries, for IBF Europe a European coproducer working with a non-European producer.
items.how_to_apply: Annual call, the next IBF Europe deadline is 15 January 2027.
items.budget_note: IBF Europe maximum EUR 40,000 per project (published)

items.name: Netherlands Film Fund (Nederlands Filmfonds)
items.summary: National agency in Amsterdam that supports Dutch feature films, documentaries, animation and shorts from development to distribution, funds minority coproductions, and runs the Netherlands Film Production Incentive cash rebate for films and high-end series.
items.eligibility: Mainly Dutch producers, foreign producers via a Dutch coproducer for minority coproductions and the incentive.
items.how_to_apply: Online through the fund's application portal, by scheme deadlines.

items.name: NPO-fonds
items.summary: Fund of the Dutch public broadcaster NPO in Hilversum for the development and production of high-quality fiction and documentary for NPO television, radio and online channels, plus podcasts and talent development projects.
items.eligibility: Only national public broadcasters (omroepen) can apply, so independent producers apply through a Dutch public broadcaster.
items.how_to_apply: Via the broadcaster's subscription process with NPO, seven advisory rounds a year.
items.budget_note: EUR 19.45 million a year, of which EUR 7.6 million for video fiction and EUR 8.06 million for video documentary in 2026 (published)

items.name: Arktisk Film Norge (Arctic Film Norway)
items.summary: Film centre, investment fund and film commission for Northern Norway, owned by Nordland, Troms and Finnmark. It gives grants for shorts, documentaries and games, and invests in features, series, feature documentaries and games with roots in the north.
items.eligibility: Norwegian independent production companies with a regional link to Nordland, Troms, Finnmark or Svalbard. A foreign lead producer needs a Northern Norwegian co-producer.
items.how_to_apply: Through Regportal. Grants on a rolling basis, investments after a dialogue with no fixed deadline.
items.budget_note: About NOK 12 million in grants in 2025, at most NOK 700,000 per project (published)

items.name: Filminvest
items.summary: Regional film fund for Trøndelag and Innlandet in Norway. It gives non-recoupable grants to productions with high regional spend and runs an investment fund that puts top financing into feature films, TV drama and games.
items.eligibility: Projects linked to the region. Foreign producers need a regional co-producer, and investments require at least 160% regional spend.
items.how_to_apply: Applications are submitted by the regional Norwegian co-producer.
items.budget_note: About EUR 1,113,000 a year in grants, investment fund about EUR 2.5 million, at most about EUR 200,000 invested per project (published)

items.name: Filmkraft Rogaland
items.summary: Regional film centre for Rogaland, owned by the county and the municipalities of Stavanger and Sandnes. It gives grants for the development and production of documentaries, fiction and short films, and for game development.

items.name: International Sámi Film Institute (ISFI)
items.summary: Film institute in Kautokeino (Guovdageaidnu) that funds Sámi film. It gives grants for script development, production, distribution and dubbing of films and series in the Sámi languages, for Sámi filmmakers across the four countries of Sápmi.
items.eligibility: Production companies with Sámi film projects. General terms and a cultural test apply.
items.how_to_apply: Through the online application system on the ISFI site.

items.name: Mediefondet Zefyr
items.summary: Regional production fund for south and west Norway, in Bergen. It invests private capital in Norwegian feature films, documentaries, TV series and games, and manages state grants for commercial film and series production linked to its six counties.
items.eligibility: Productions linked to Møre og Romsdal, Vestland, Rogaland, Agder, Telemark or Vestfold.
items.how_to_apply: Investments by individual negotiation, start with the production adviser. Grants on a rolling basis, decided at board meetings, apply at least six weeks before.

items.name: Midtnorsk Filmsenter
items.summary: Regional film centre for central Norway in Trondheim. It gives development and production grants to documentaries, documentary series, short films, feature films, drama series and games, including international co-productions.
items.how_to_apply: Grants are decided in application rounds by the board.

items.name: Nordisk Film & TV Fond
items.summary: Nordic fund in Oslo, governed by a board appointed by the Nordic Council of Ministers. Top-finances Nordic feature films, drama series and creative documentaries, and supports distribution and dubbing of Nordic films in other Nordic countries.
items.eligibility: Nordic production companies acting as delegate producer, with national base funding confirmed, at least 70% of financing in place and distribution in at least two Nordic countries.
items.how_to_apply: Online through the NFTVF application portal, before principal photography for fiction and at least 12 weeks before locked edit for documentaries.
items.budget_note: About NOK 130 million budget for 2026 (published)

items.name: Norwegian Film Institute (Norsk filminstitutt)
items.summary: The state film body of Norway, in Oslo. It funds the development, production, promotion and distribution of Norwegian films, series and games, and gives co-production grants to Norwegian minority co-producers of foreign features and documentaries.
items.eligibility: Norwegian production companies. Foreign producers apply for co-production funding through a Norwegian co-producer.

items.name: Oslo Filmfond
items.summary: City-owned fund for film and series production in the Oslo region, also managing investment money from Buskerud. It gives grants and invests as co-producer in feature films and series with a link to Oslo or Buskerud.
items.eligibility: Productions with story and shooting in Oslo and/or Buskerud. Investments need about 80% of the budget secured and a confirmed distributor or platform.
items.how_to_apply: Contact the fund first, then apply through the site. All current grant and investment funds were allocated at the time of reading.

items.name: Østnorsk Filmsenter (Eastern Norway Film Center)
items.summary: Regional funding centre for film and games in Innlandet county, in Lillehammer. It funds development, production and co-production of short films, documentaries, games and interactive media.
items.eligibility: Projects with a co-producer based in Innlandet and real use of regional professionals.
items.how_to_apply: The regional co-producer applies digitally through Regportal.

items.name: Sørnorsk Filmsenter
items.summary: Regional film centre for Agder, Vestfold and Telemark in southern Norway. It gives grants to professional filmmakers, game developers and producers in the region.
items.eligibility: Professional filmmakers, game developers or producers who live and work in Agder, Vestfold or Telemark. No grants for students or post-production.
items.how_to_apply: Three deadlines a year (in 2026: 11 January, 11 April, 11 September), through Regportal with BankID.

items.name: Vestnorsk Filmsenter (Western Norway Film Fund)
items.summary: Regional film fund for Vestland and Møre og Romsdal, in Bergen. It funds development and production of feature films, drama series, documentaries and short fiction, plus games.
items.eligibility: Applicants with address and main business in Vestland or Møre og Romsdal. Production grants go to limited companies whose main purpose is audiovisual production.
items.how_to_apply: Separate calls and deadlines per scheme. Feature and drama production grants are announced separately.

items.name: Viken Filmsenter
items.summary: Regional film centre for Buskerud, Akershus, Østfold and Oslo. It supports development and co-production of short films, documentaries and games, including regional and international collaborations.
items.how_to_apply: No application deadlines.
items.budget_note: About NOK 13 million in grants (published)

items.name: Gdańsk Film Fund (Gdański Fundusz Filmowy)
items.summary: City of Gdańsk fund within the Institute of Urban Culture. It co-produces and jointly exploits fiction, documentary and animated films, and also runs a short film competition (Short Lab) and a script competition (Gdańsk Script).
items.eligibility: Producers of feature (over 70 minutes), documentary or animated films that promote Gdańsk.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly production competition, plus separate calls for Short Lab and Gdańsk Script.

items.name: Gdynia Film Fund (Gdyński Fundusz Filmowy)
items.summary: City of Gdynia programme operated by the Gdynia Film Centre. Set up in 2008 and relaunched in 2026, it supports production and post-production of projects linked to Gdynia, with a focus on short films.
items.eligibility: Filmmakers and producers with projects tied to Gdynia by subject or shooting location.
items.how_to_apply: Competition announced by the Gdynia Film Centre.

items.name: Kraków Film Fund (Fundusz Filmowy w Krakowie)
items.summary: City of Kraków fund operated by the Krakow Festival Office (KBF, Krakow Film Commission). KBF co-produces fiction, documentary and animated films linked to Kraków and Małopolska and takes a proportional share of rights and revenues.
items.eligibility: Any company able to make the film, with at least 5% own contribution and a closed financing plan. KBF pays at most 50% of production costs and the producer spends 150% of it in Małopolska.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly competition, application uploaded online (2026 window 4 to 25 May).

items.name: Łódź Film Fund (Łódzki Fundusz Filmowy)
items.summary: Poland's oldest regional film fund, run by EC1 Łódź (Łódź Film Commission) and paid for by the City of Łódź. It co-produces fiction, documentary and animated films linked to Łódź and its region, taking a share in rights and revenues.
items.eligibility: Projects connected to Łódź or the Łódź voivodeship through the filmmakers, the subject or the shooting location.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly competition run by EC1 Łódź.
items.budget_note: PLN 1.5 million gross for the 2026 competition (published)

items.name: Lower Silesian and Wrocław Film Fund (Dolnośląski i Wrocławski Fundusz Filmowy)
items.summary: Fund of the Lower Silesia region and the City of Wrocław, operated by the Lower Silesian Film Centre (formerly Odra-Film). Through a yearly competition it co-produces fiction, documentary and animated films tied to Lower Silesia and Wrocław.
items.eligibility: Projects linked to Lower Silesia and Wrocław through shooting locations and local crew and companies.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly competition, usually announced in the first half of the year (the 2026 call ran from late May).
items.budget_note: Almost PLN 2,400,000 for the 2026 edition (published)

items.name: Małopolska Film Fund for Short Forms (Małopolski Fundusz Filmowy Małych Form)
