items.summary: Competition run by the Krakow Festival Office with money from Kraków and the Małopolska region. It gives awards to low-budget short fiction, documentary and animated films linked to Kraków or Małopolska, often first films.
items.eligibility: Short films up to 45 minutes with a budget up to PLN 400,000 net, linked to Kraków or Małopolska. Winners sign a licence agreement with KBF.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly competition announced on the Krakow Film Commission website.
items.budget_note: Awards of PLN 50,000 to 100,000 net (category A) or below PLN 50,000 net (category B) (published)

items.name: Mazovia and Warsaw Film Fund (Mazowiecki i Warszawski Fundusz Filmowy)
items.summary: Regional fund run by the Mazovian Institute of Culture in Warsaw. Through a yearly competition it joins fiction, documentary and animated films linked to Warsaw and the Mazovia region as a co-producer with a financial contribution.
items.eligibility: Film production companies with a project tied to Warsaw or Mazovia. The fund pays at most 50% of production costs and the producer must spend 150% of the award in the region.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly competition with an electronic application form, deadline for the 2026 edition was 19 February 2026.
items.budget_note: PLN 3.2 million gross for the 16th edition (published)

items.name: Podkarpackie Regional Film Fund (Podkarpacki Regionalny Fundusz Filmowy)
items.summary: Fund of the Podkarpackie region, run by the Podkarpackie Film Commission at the Regional Culture Centre in Rzeszów. The centre co-produces films and series linked to the region by subject, local crew or, above all, shooting location.
items.eligibility: Film production companies active for at least a year before the call. At least 100% of the net contribution must be spent in Podkarpackie.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly competition under published rules (regulamin).
items.budget_note: PLN 1,300,000 gross for 2026 (published)

items.name: Polish Film Institute (PISF)
items.summary: Poland's national film body in Warsaw. Its yearly operational programmes fund the development and production of Polish features, debuts, documentaries, animation and minority co-productions, plus distribution of Polish films.
items.eligibility: Companies whose business is film production (individuals only for script grants), under the yearly operational programmes.
items.how_to_apply: Through the PISF online application system during fixed call sessions each year.
items.budget_note: Film production programme allocation for 2026 up to PLN 173,450,000 (published)

items.name: Silesian Film Fund (Śląski Fundusz Filmowy, Silesia Film)
items.summary: Fund of the Silesia Film institution in Katowice. It becomes co-producer, with a financial stake, of features, shorts, documentaries and animation tied to the Silesian voivodeship by theme or shooting location. Returns flow back into the fund.
items.eligibility: Projects linked to the Silesian voivodeship by subject or by where they are shot.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly call (nabór) announced on the Silesia Film website.

items.name: Warmia-Masuria Film Fund (Warmińsko-Mazurski Fundusz Filmowy)
items.summary: Regional fund in Olsztyn, paid for by the Warmia-Masuria regional government and run from its Centre for Education and Cultural Initiatives. It funds fiction and documentary films shot in and connected to Warmia and Masuria.
items.eligibility: Productions tied to Warmia and Masuria through locations, subject, characters or local crew and companies, with part of the budget spent in the region.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly competition with formal, expert and committee stages (the 11th call closed on 31 August 2026).

items.name: West Pomeranian Film Fund Pomerania Film (Zachodniopomorski Fundusz Filmowy Pomerania Film)
items.summary: Fund of the West Pomeranian region and the cities of Szczecin and Koszalin, based at the Pomeranian Dukes' Castle in Szczecin. It co-produces films, series and shorts connected to the region, taking a share of rights and revenues.
items.eligibility: Productions linked to West Pomerania, with at least 5 shooting days in the region. Covers up to 50% of costs for fiction and series, up to 75% for documentary, animation and shorts.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly competition with an online form and published rules.
items.budget_note: PLN 650,000 shared among 9 projects in the 18th competition (published)

items.name: ICA (Instituto do Cinema e do Audiovisual)
items.summary: Portugal's national film and audiovisual institute in Lisbon. Its yearly calls fund writing and development, first features and documentaries, fiction and animated shorts, audiovisual fiction, documentary and animation, distribution and international promotion.
items.eligibility: Producers must first be validated by ICA as independent producers before they can enter the calls.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly calls (concursos), applications through ICA's online platform.
items.budget_note: Writing and development of cinematographic works 2026: EUR 650,000 in total, up to EUR 500,000 for a slate (published)

items.name: Romanian National Cinema Centre (Centrul Național al Cinematografiei, CNC)
items.summary: Romania's national film body in Bucharest. It runs competitions for cinema projects with development and production credits, and gives non-refundable support for artistic quality, audience success, distribution and festival participation.
items.eligibility: Romanian producers registered in the Cinematography Register, under the competition rules (Order 2335/2006).
items.how_to_apply: Competition sessions for cinema projects with online registration, non-refundable requests uploaded to the SDFC platform before Board meetings.

items.name: Film Center Serbia (Filmski centar Srbije, FCS)
items.summary: Serbia's national film institution in Belgrade. Through open competitions it co-finances script and project development and the production of Serbian features, debuts, documentaries, animated shorts, student films and minority co-productions, plus distribution.
items.eligibility: Producers of Serbian films and Serbian minority co-producers, as set in each competition.
items.how_to_apply: Open competitions announced in a yearly calendar (spring cycle in April in 2024). No competition was open when checked.

items.name: Slovak Audiovisual Fund (Audiovizuálny fond, AVF)
items.summary: Public fund in Bratislava set up by law in 2009 and paid for by the state and by broadcasters, cinemas and distributors. It gives grants, loans and scholarships for the development, production and distribution of Slovak works and co-productions with a Slovak share.
items.eligibility: Authors and producers of Slovak audiovisual works, and Slovak producers with a share in a co-production, registered in the fund's system.
items.how_to_apply: Calls (výzvy) published each year under the fund's structure of support, applications through the registration system.

items.name: Slovenian Film Centre (Slovenski filmski center, SFC)
items.summary: Public agency of the Republic of Slovenia in Ljubljana, successor of the Slovenian Film Fund. Through public tenders and calls it co-finances script and project development, production, distribution and promotion of Slovenian films and audiovisual works.
items.eligibility: Set per tender. For most development and production tenders projects must come through a producer who meets the criteria.
items.how_to_apply: Only through public tenders and calls, by the procedure and deadline in each call.

items.name: AGADIC (Axencia Galega das Industrias Culturais)
items.summary: Cultural industries agency of the Galician government in Santiago de Compostela, with grants for producing and co-producing Galician audiovisual projects, for development, and for shoots in Galicia.
items.how_to_apply: Online through the Xunta de Galicia e-office. In 2026 production ran from 29 January to 2 March and development from 24 July to 24 August.
items.budget_note: 2026: EUR 3,500,000 for production and co-production, EUR 1,200,000 for development, EUR 2,533,000 for shoots in Galicia (published)

items.name: Agencia Andaluza de Instituciones Culturales (Junta de Andalucía)
items.summary: Cultural agency of the Andalusian government in Seville. Its yearly call funds fiction and animated features and TV films, with a line for new directors, and documentaries.
items.eligibility: Independent production companies registered for audiovisual production. The documentary line is also open to individuals.
items.how_to_apply: Online during the yearly call, the 2026 window ran from 10 to 30 July 2026.
items.budget_note: 2026: EUR 5,215,000 in total, up to EUR 450,000 per feature (EUR 300,000 for new directors) and EUR 125,000 per documentary (published)

items.name: Basque Government audiovisual grants (Gobierno Vasco)
items.summary: Grants from the Basque Government for developing projects and producing fiction features, animated features, creative documentaries, shorts and series in Basque, with part of each budget kept for work in Basque.
items.eligibility: Independent private producers established in the EU or EEA, who must open a permanent establishment in the Basque Country if they receive a grant.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly calls per line, applications through euskadi.eus.
items.budget_note: 2026 production calls: EUR 8,828,000 in total, of which EUR 3,200,000 for fiction features and EUR 3,000,000 for series in Basque (published)

items.name: Comunidad de Madrid audiovisual grants
items.summary: Grants from the Madrid regional government for feature production (including a line for first and second time directors), short films and the development of features and series.
items.eligibility: Independent production companies based in the Madrid region. Short film grants are for micro and small companies with tax residence in Madrid, development grants need two years of audiovisual experience.
items.budget_note: Short films: up to EUR 24,000 for fiction, EUR 30,000 for animation and EUR 18,000 for documentary (published)

items.name: CREA SGR
items.summary: Non profit mutual guarantee company near Madrid for the cultural and audiovisual sector. It guarantees bank loans to producers and other audiovisual companies, so banks lend on better terms.
items.eligibility: SMEs and self-employed professionals in audiovisual production, post-production, distribution and exhibition, with at least one employee and no tax or social security arrears.
items.how_to_apply: Online application for a guarantee through creasgronline.com.

items.name: ICAA (Instituto de la Cinematografía y de las Artes Audiovisuales)
items.summary: Spain's national film institute in Madrid, part of the Ministry of Culture. It gives grants for screenwriting, general and selective feature production, short films, and national and international distribution.
items.eligibility: Selective production grants are for independent production companies, with room for documentaries, new directors and experimental projects.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly calls per aid line, published on the Ministry of Culture website.
items.budget_note: Selective feature production 2025: up to EUR 17 million in total, up to EUR 800,000 per project and EUR 1,000,000 for animation (published)

items.name: ICEC (Institut Català de les Empreses Culturals)
items.summary: Cultural industries agency of the Catalan government in Barcelona. It gives grants for development and for producing features, series, documentaries, animation and shorts, minority co-productions, and repayable support for feature distribution.
items.eligibility: Depends on the call. The repayable distribution support is for companies and non profits based in Catalonia that have operated for at least two years.
items.how_to_apply: Separate calls listed in the ICEC grants calendar, applications through the Generalitat's online procedures.

items.name: ICO (Instituto de Crédito Oficial), audiovisual line with RTVE
items.summary: Spain's public credit institution in Madrid. Under an agreement with RTVE it finances the production of features, shorts, TV series and documentaries in which the public broadcaster takes part.
items.eligibility: Productions in which RTVE participates.
items.budget_note: EUR 200 million over four years under the RTVE agreement (published)

items.name: Institut Valencià de Cultura (IVC)
items.summary: Cultural institute of the Valencian government in Valencia, with yearly grants for screenwriting and development and for producing audiovisual works, plus a line for documentaries on living traditions.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly calls, the production call for 2026 to 2028 closed on 27 March 2026.

items.name: Instituto Canario de Desarrollo Cultural (ICDC)
items.summary: Cultural institute of the Canary Islands government in Las Palmas. It funds production and minority co-production of fiction, animated and documentary features and series, development of features and series, and short films.
items.eligibility: Audiovisual production companies and self-employed producers.
items.how_to_apply: Yearly calls, the 2026 production and co-production call closed on 3 August 2026 and the development and shorts call on 11 September 2026.
items.budget_note: Up to EUR 225,000 per fiction or animated feature or series and EUR 140,000 per documentary, minority co-productions up to EUR 165,000 and EUR 100,000 (published)

items.name: Madrid City Council film grants (Madrid Film Office)
items.summary: Grants from the city of Madrid, presented by the Madrid Film Office, for producing and for distributing fiction features (including animation) and documentaries linked to Madrid.
items.eligibility: Fiction and documentary feature productions linked to Madrid.
items.how_to_apply: Production applications each year from 1 February to 31 March, distribution from 15 to 31 January and 15 to 30 June.
items.budget_note: Production: EUR 2,000,000 a year, up to EUR 100,000 per fiction feature and EUR 60,000 per documentary (published)

items.name: Film i Dalarna
items.summary: Regional film centre for Dalarna. It co-produces and part-owns feature films, short films, documentaries and fiction series, with features and series shot in the region since 2022.
items.eligibility: A company with a Swedish organisation number and documented production experience. No support for development.
items.how_to_apply: Three or four application dates a year, decision two to four weeks after each date.
items.budget_note: Shorts and documentaries usually SEK 20,000 to 70,000 (published)

items.name: Film i Skåne
items.summary: Regional film centre for Skåne in southern Sweden, based in Ystad. It co-produces feature fiction, drama series, documentaries and short fiction made in the region, taking rights and a share of revenues, and also funds development.
items.eligibility: Only Swedish producers with a production company may apply. Spending in Skåne is required, and international minority co-productions apply through a Swedish producer.
items.how_to_apply: Rolling applications through the online form, decision by the production group in about six weeks.
items.budget_note: At most 30% of a project's budget (published)

items.name: Film i Väst
items.summary: Regional film fund for Västra Götaland, based in Trollhättan. It invests in, part-owns and co-produces Swedish and international feature films, documentaries, short formats and drama series that shoot or post-produce in the region.
items.eligibility: Production companies whose project places part of the shoot or post-production in Västra Götaland, with at least 100 percent of the investment spent there.
items.how_to_apply: Application via the Film i Väst application portal, decision by the production group within six weeks.

items.name: Film i Västerbotten
items.summary: Regional resource centre for film in Västerbotten county, part of Region Västerbotten in Umeå. It co-produces short films and documentaries.

items.name: Film Stockholm
items.summary: Regional film fund for the Stockholm region, owned by Region Stockholm and run with the City of Stockholm. It invests as co-producer in feature films, TV drama, short films and documentaries made wholly or partly in the region.
items.eligibility: All or part of the production must take place in the Stockholm region.
items.how_to_apply: Through the Film Stockholm application portal.

items.name: Film Västernorrland
items.summary: Regional film centre for Västernorrland county. It co-produces short films and documentaries each year and, since 2022, feature films and TV drama shot wholly or partly in the county, taking a share of ownership.
items.eligibility: Features and drama must shoot wholly or partly in Västernorrland. Shorts and documentaries need a filmmaker who lives in or comes from the county, or production there.
items.how_to_apply: Feature and drama applications on a rolling basis. Shorts and documentaries three deadlines a year (15 February, 15 April, 15 October).
items.budget_note: SEK 6 million in total per year, of which SEK 5 million for features and TV drama. Shorts and documentaries at most SEK 100,000 (published)

items.name: Filmpool Nord
items.summary: Regional film company for Norrbotten in the far north of Sweden. It co-produces short fiction, documentaries, feature films and TV drama, with a claim on rights and returns.
items.how_to_apply: Applications for documentary, short fiction, feature film and TV drama through the online application portal.

items.name: Gotland Film Fund (Gotlands filmfond)
items.summary: Fund for feature films, drama series and feature documentaries shot on the island of Gotland. Applications are handled by Film Stockholm, and the Kustateljén studio in Fårösund can be offered as well.
items.eligibility: Projects to be shot on Gotland.
items.how_to_apply: Through the Film Stockholm application portal.
items.budget_note: SEK 3 million per year for co-production and development (published)

items.name: Swedish Film Institute (Svenska Filminstitutet)
items.summary: The state film body of Sweden, based in Stockholm. It funds the development and production of Swedish feature fiction, documentaries and short films, minority co-productions with a foreign lead producer, and the international launch of Swedish films.
items.eligibility: Producers and production companies making Swedish films, plus Swedish companies co-producing with a foreign lead producer.
items.how_to_apply: Through the online application service, with decisions by film commissioners (filmkonsulenter).

items.name: Aargauer Kuratorium, film department
items.summary: Arts council of the canton of Aargau whose film department supports fiction, documentary and experimental films and media art by professional Aargau filmmakers in development, production and distribution, plus individual work grants.
items.eligibility: Professional filmmakers from Aargau. TV films and TV productions without a release plan beyond television are excluded, as are student films except graduation films.

items.name: Berner Filmförderung (Canton of Bern film funding)
items.summary: Film support of the canton of Bern for professional auteur film. It funds project development in two stages, production and film distribution, aiming at films with national and international reach from the canton.
items.eligibility: Authors and directors resident in the canton of Bern for at least two years, or production companies headquartered there for two years, with planned spending in the canton of at least 150 percent of the grant.
items.how_to_apply: Online application portal, four fixed deadlines a year (for example 23 October 2026), usually before the shoot starts.
items.budget_note: Production grant up to 50 percent of recognised costs (published)

items.name: Cinéforom (Fondation romande pour le cinéma)
items.summary: Film foundation of French-speaking Switzerland, funded by the cantons of Geneva, Vaud, Valais, Neuchâtel, Fribourg and Jura, cities and the Loterie Romande. It gives selective aid, automatic complementary support for writing and production, support for digital experiences and distribution aid.
items.eligibility: Production companies registered in Cinéforom's company register, working in French-speaking Switzerland.
items.how_to_apply: Four selective sessions a year (2026 deadlines: 12 January, 20 April, 13 July, 5 October), the commission meets six to seven weeks later.
items.budget_note: Budget of around CHF 10 million (published)

items.name: Fachausschuss Film und Medienkunst BS/BL (Basel film funding)
items.summary: Joint film and media art committee of the cantons Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft. It funds script and project development for fiction features and long documentaries, production of films, and media art projects.
items.eligibility: Writers and directors resident in Basel-Stadt or Basel-Landschaft for at least a year, independent production companies based there for two years, or other Swiss producers working with a Basel-based writer or director.
items.how_to_apply: Applications to the committee, which meets three times a year, managed by the Basel-Stadt culture department.
items.budget_note: Development grants usually CHF 10,000 to 30,000 (published)

items.name: Kulturfonds Suissimage (Suissimage Cultural Fund)
items.summary: Foundation of the Swiss collecting society Suissimage in Bern. It tops up production of Swiss cinema fiction and documentaries already backed by the Federal Office of Culture or SRG SSR, and with the SSA fund supports writing of series.
items.eligibility: Swiss cinema projects ready to shoot with confirmed support from the Federal Office of Culture or SRG SSR (Pacte de l'Audiovisuel), series writing support for Swiss screenwriters.
items.how_to_apply: Application form from the website or Suissimage secretariat, by the published meeting dates.
items.budget_note: Series writing programme of CHF 200,000 a year with the SSA fund (published)

items.name: St. Gallen cantonal film funding (St.Galler Filmförderung)
items.summary: Film support of the canton of St. Gallen for projects with a clear link to the canton, covering content and project development, production, post-production and distribution, plus a treatment competition every two years.
items.eligibility: Mainly St. Gallen filmmakers or production companies, or projects with a substantial St. Gallen subject.
items.how_to_apply: Digital application forms per project phase, assessed by the cantonal film commission.

items.name: Swiss Federal Office of Culture, film funding (BAK / OFC)
items.summary: Film department of the Swiss federal government in Bern. It runs selective support for screenplay and production (plus project development for documentaries and animation), success-based support (Succès Cinéma) and the FiSS location incentive, and handles minority coproductions.
items.eligibility: Swiss production companies, minority coproductions without a lead Swiss company are assessed by individual experts with a points system.
items.how_to_apply: Online through the federal eSubventions portal, by the expert commission's meeting calendar and before production starts.

items.name: Teleproduktions-Fonds (Fonds de production télévisuelle)
items.summary: Fund in Bern set up by the Swiss collecting societies Swissperform, Suissimage and SSA. It co-finances script development and production of TV fiction, documentaries, series and animation by independent Swiss producers, as conditionally repayable loans.
items.eligibility: Independent Swiss production companies (no broadcaster stake) based in Switzerland for at least two years, in a Swiss national language, with a broadcaster contributing at least CHF 50,000 for production aid (not for animation).
items.how_to_apply: Online via eTPF, fiction on a rolling basis with decisions within about a month, documentaries on the Federal Office of Culture deadlines.
items.budget_note: Usually up to CHF 300,000 for fiction films and series, CHF 50,000 for documentaries and CHF 100,000 for documentary series (published)

items.name: Ticino Film Commission production incentives
items.summary: Film commission of Italian-speaking Switzerland in Locarno. It gives financial incentives that partly cover local spending from preproduction to post-production, support for development and distribution of films partly in Italian, and access to the Locarno, Mendrisio and Airolo regional film funds.
items.eligibility: Production companies based in Switzerland or abroad that shoot in Ticino, assessed project by project on set criteria.
items.how_to_apply: Contact the commission, rules and spending tables for each scheme are on the incentives page.
items.budget_note: Airolo Film Fund up to CHF 20,000 a year (published)

items.name: Zentralschweizer Filmförderung (Central Switzerland film funding)
items.summary: Joint film funding of the six Central Swiss cantons, based in Lucerne. It supports fiction, documentary, animation, experimental and short films, series and transmedia projects through development, production, post-production, promotion and distribution.
items.eligibility: Filmmakers and projects linked to the Central Swiss cantons, under shared guidelines and information sheets.
items.how_to_apply: Online platform, four deadlines a year (next: 15 October 2026, 11 January 2027), distribution requests on a rolling basis. A commission with one delegate per canton decides.

items.name: Zürcher Filmstiftung (Zurich Film Foundation)
items.summary: Film fund of the canton and city of Zürich for professional fiction, non-fiction and animation, from screenwriting and development to production and marketing, plus a digital culture strand for interactive works.
items.eligibility: Screenwriters, production and distribution companies active in the canton of Zürich and independent of broadcasters, writers need two years of tax residence in the canton.
items.how_to_apply: Online platform by fixed submission dates per expert commission, no extensions.
items.budget_note: CHF 10,396,638 awarded in 2025 (published)

items.name: BFI Doc Society Fund (Doc Society)
items.summary: Non-profit Doc Society distributes the BFI's National Lottery money for documentary, with non-recoupable grants for the development, production and completion of UK non-fiction features, short documentaries and immersive projects.
items.eligibility: UK filmmakers and producers with non-fiction feature, short or immersive projects, funded once per stage.
items.how_to_apply: Online, all year round for the feature production fund, in two stages: an Expression of Interest, then an invited full application.
items.budget_note: Feature development grants £25,000 to £40,000, production and completion grants up to £150,000 per film, short documentaries up to £25,000 (published)

items.name: British Film Institute (BFI Filmmaking Fund)
items.summary: The UK's lead body for film awards National Lottery money for the development and production of live action and animated features, international co-productions, short films through BFI NETWORK and immersive projects.
items.eligibility: Producers applying through a limited company registered at Companies House, with separate strands for debut and experienced directors.
items.how_to_apply: Online application linked from the fund guidelines. Development and Impact feature funding are open on a rolling basis, Discovery feature funding works in rounds.
items.budget_note: Discovery awards up to £1,000,000 and Impact awards up to £1,250,000 per feature (published)

items.name: Calculus Capital (Alchemy funds)
items.summary: London fund manager whose Alchemy and Alchemy Plus funds invest in companies that make senior loans to film and TV productions, secured against programme orders, tax credits and sales contracts, and in the Plus fund also against unsold rights (gap).

items.name: Coutts (Media Banking)
items.summary: London private and commercial bank with a media team that banks production companies and lends to film and TV productions against pre-sales, broadcaster commissions and tax credits, including some overseas rebates.

items.name: Creative Wales (Production Funding)
items.summary: Welsh Government agency for the creative industries. Its Production Funding gives mostly non-repayable awards to film, TV, games and animation productions made wholly or partly in Wales, and it co-funds the Sinema Cymru Welsh language feature scheme.
items.eligibility: Film, TV, games or animation companies with a production made at least partly in Wales, all other funding in place, a commercial deal, a skills element and a recent commercial release.
items.how_to_apply: Expression of interest at least 12 weeks before the project starts, after reading the Production Funding guidance.
items.budget_note: Awards of £50,000 to £750,000 for scripted and £50,000 to £300,000 for non-scripted productions (published)

items.name: Ffilm Cymru Wales
items.summary: Development agency for Welsh film in Cardiff. Funds short films and the development and production of live action, documentary and animated features led by Wales born or based writers, directors and producers, with a mix of grant and recoupable equity.
items.eligibility: Teams with Wales born or based talent as lead writer, producer or director, applying through a UK registered company and able to close financing within six months.
items.how_to_apply: Expression of interest form by email, then an invited full application. Awards of £50,000 or more go to scheduled board meetings.
items.budget_note: Production awards up to £600,000, most between £150,000 and £400,000, normally no more than 50% of the budget (published)

items.name: Film London
items.summary: Screen agency for London. Runs BFI NETWORK support for new filmmakers in the capital and the FLAMIN schemes, which commission and fund moving image works and animations by artists based in England.
items.eligibility: New and emerging filmmakers (BFI NETWORK) and early or mid-career artist filmmakers based in England (FLAMIN).
items.how_to_apply: Annual open calls for the FLAMIN schemes, announced through the FLAMIN newsletter and the Film London website.

items.name: Head Gear Films
items.summary: Independent film financier that cashflows government incentives such as the UK rebate, lends against pre-sale contracts and provides gap funding for independent films, TV series and games, and helps package projects.
items.eligibility: Producers with a project and a finance plan. No unsolicited materials are accepted.
items.how_to_apply: Enquiry form on the website stating project type, finance plan, sales agent and the type of financing needed.

items.name: Liverpool City Region Production Fund (Liverpool Film Office)
items.summary: Production fund managed by the Liverpool Film Office that invests in feature films and scripted TV filmed in Liverpool and the surrounding city region, normally as recoupable equity with a share of net profits.
items.eligibility: Local, national and international production companies with live action, animated or documentary features or scripted TV made in the Liverpool City Region. Unscripted TV, web series and games are excluded.
items.how_to_apply: Read the guidelines, then submit an Expression of Interest through the Liverpool Film Office website.
items.budget_note: £100,000 to £500,000 per project, normally no more than 20% of the production budget (published)

items.name: Media Finance Capital (MFC)
items.summary: London company backed by Dorfman Media Holdings that provides structured debt to independent film and TV productions against tax credits, rebates, grants, pre-sales, broadcaster and streaming licence fees, and offers executive producing services.
items.eligibility: Packaged film and TV projects with commercial appeal, an identifiable audience and a sound financial structure.
items.how_to_apply: Submission by email with script, budget, schedule, finance plan, talent, sales estimates, tax credit estimate and bond company.

items.name: MONET
items.summary: London finance platform for media companies offering production financing for film and high-end TV against tax credits, pre-sales and broadcaster and streamer licence fees, plus revolving credit for production companies.
items.eligibility: Film and HETV projects, typically with budgets of £2m to £20m.
items.how_to_apply: Online application on the website.
items.budget_note: Production financing up to £20m per project, revolving facilities from £75,000 to £3m (published)

items.name: North East Screen (North East Production Fund)
items.summary: Screen agency for North East England. Its North East Production Fund invests in commissioned high-end TV drama and commercial feature films that spend in the region and hire local crew and suppliers.
items.eligibility: Commissioned HETV drama and commercial feature films that commit to regional spend, North East supply chain companies and local jobs.
items.how_to_apply: Read the guidelines, then submit an Expression of Interest. Applications are assessed by independent experts and decided by an investment panel.

items.name: Northern Ireland Screen
items.summary: Screen agency for Northern Ireland in Belfast. Funds development and production of feature films, TV drama, animation, factual TV and interactive content with economic benefit to the region, and runs the Irish Language and Ulster-Scots Broadcast Funds.
items.eligibility: Legally incorporated companies that meet the British cultural criteria and project criteria, with at least 65% of production funding in place.
items.how_to_apply: Start by contacting the Head of Production to discuss the project, who indicates the level of funding that can be applied for.

items.name: Principal Film Finance
items.summary: Film production and financing company in Bristol and London that cashflows tax credits and pre-sales and provides gap finance against unsold territories, alongside executive producing services. Part of the Happy Hour Media Group.
items.how_to_apply: Contact by email via the website.

items.name: Screen Cornwall (SCEPI)
items.summary: Screen agency for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. Its equity fund SCEPI, backed by Cornwall Council and private investors, invests as recoupable senior equity in feature films, scripted TV and immersive projects that shoot in the region.
items.eligibility: Experienced producers with live action or animated features, scripted TV drama or comedy, or paid immersive projects that shoot in Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly, with at least 50% of funding confirmed.
items.how_to_apply: Expression of Interest form after reading the guidelines and FAQ. Full application by invitation only.
items.budget_note: Up to £500,000 per project at a minimum 4 to 1 spend ratio (published)

items.name: Screen Scotland
items.summary: Screen agency for Scotland, part of Creative Scotland, funding the development and production of feature films and documentaries by Scotland-based filmmakers, plus development and production of TV programmes through its Broadcast Content Fund.
items.eligibility: Producers, writers and directors based in Scotland, or projects with Scotland-based writing or directing talent.
items.how_to_apply: Rolling applications with no deadlines, after first completing the BFI Diversity Standards step on the BFI portal.
items.budget_note: Development awards £3,000 to £50,000 and film production awards £100,000 to £500,000 (published)

items.name: Screen Yorkshire (Yorkshire Content Fund)
items.summary: Screen agency for Yorkshire and the Humber. Its Yorkshire Content Fund is a public-private investment fund for film, TV, games and digital projects made in or connected to the region.
items.eligibility: Producers based in Yorkshire, or producers who will film in the region or set up a base there.
items.how_to_apply: Application following the published Yorkshire Content Fund guidelines, with help available from the Screen Yorkshire team.
items.budget_note: Up to £500,000 per project (published)
